subject: general
question: The potential energy acquired by a balloon when we press it (changing its shape), or by a spring inside a toy car when wound, is possessed by virtue of the object's ____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**configuration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy** is defined as the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **position** relative to others, **stresses** within itself, its **electric charge**, or its **configuration**.
 
• When we press a **balloon**, we apply an **external force** that changes its **shape**. This change in **physical arrangement** or **configuration** stores energy within the balloon's material. ***Hence, the mention of changing shape relates directly to configuration.***
 
• A **spring** inside a **toy car**, when **wound**, undergoes a change in its **coiling structure**. The work done in winding the spring is stored as **Elastic Potential Energy** due to the altered **configuration** of the metal coils.
 
• The term **configuration** in physics refers to the **relative positions** of the constituent particles of a system or the **geometrical shape** of an object.
 
• This energy remains **stored** as long as the object is held in that specific state and is **released** when the object is allowed to return to its original form, often converting into **Kinetic Energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Potential Energy:**
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy**: This is energy stored in an object due to its **vertical position** or **height**. The **numerical value** is calculated using the formula **P.E. = mgh**, where **m** is **mass**, **g** is **acceleration due to gravity** (approx **9.8 m/s²**), and **h** is **height**.
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy**: Stored in materials that can be **stretched** or **compressed**, such as **rubber bands**, **trampolines**, or **springs**.
 
• **Chemical Potential Energy**: Stored in the **chemical bonds** of substances, like in **batteries**, **food**, or **fuel**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• This is the energy of **motion**. An object moving at a **constant speed** possesses kinetic energy defined by the **mass** and the **square of its velocity** (**K.E. = 1/2 mv²**).
 
• Unlike potential energy, kinetic energy cannot be stored; it is **actively used** during motion.
 
 
 
• **Mechanical Energy:**
 
 
• The **sum** of potential and kinetic energy in a system is called **Mechanical Energy**. According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, the total mechanical energy in an **isolated system** remains **constant**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Configuration vs. Position:** While **position** usually refers to the **location** of an object in a **gravitational field**, **configuration** refers to the **internal arrangement** or **deformation** of the object itself.
 
• **Unit of Energy:** The **S.I. unit** of energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**. One Joule is equal to the **work done** by a **force** of **one Newton** acting through a **distance** of **one meter**.
 
• **Factors affecting Elastic Potential Energy:** It depends on the **spring constant (k)**, which represents the **stiffness** of the material, and the **displacement (x)** or the amount of **deformation** applied.
 
• **Historical Context:** The concept of **Potential Energy** was formally introduced in the **19th century** by the Scottish engineer and physicist **William Rankine**.
